stem: One container remains saturated much longer than neighboring comparable containers. What should the technician do?
choices: Classify the whole room as overwatered because one container stays wet longer than its neighbors.
Add fertilizer to the wet container so plant demand increases and moisture is used faster.
Leave the container until the next crop cycle because one localized abnormality does not justify action.
Document the localized saturation pattern, verify permitted delivery/root-zone checks for that container, and escalate if the abnormality remains unresolved.
rationale: A single container staying wet much longer than comparable neighbors is a localized pattern, not proof that the whole room is overwatered. Possible contributors include delivery, drainage, media condition, root function, or measurement differences. Technician I should document the contrast, complete only assigned checks, and escalate if the cause remains unresolved.
